articles.title: October fest on Dalal Street: Sensex rises 1.5k points as bulls return
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Sensex and Nifty rallied sharply on Thursday even as most Asian markets were deep in the red as investors said that India’s relatively lower
articles.body: MUMBAI: Sensex and Nifty rallied sharply on Thursday even as most Asian markets were deep in the red as investors said that India’s relatively lower valuation compared to its global peers could bring foreign funds back into the domestic market.The gains came despite strong foreign fund selling but aided by some end-of-the-session short covering by speculators who wanted to cut their losses, market players said. A steady rupee and marginal softening of crude prices also helped the rally.With bulls on Dalal Street in charge of the day’s session, sensex closed 1,534 points or 2.1% up at 74,316 points while Nifty was up 375 points or 1.7% at 22,997 points. In comparison, Kospi in South Korea was down 8%, Nikkei in Japan closed 4.9% down, while Shanghai Composite closed 1.6% down.According to Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments, Indian markets rallied sharply as concerns over stretched AI valuations and higher US inflation triggered a sell-off across tech-heavy global markets, improving India’s relative appeal and encouraging rotation toward domestic large-cap technology, private financials and defensive heavyweights.“Correcting bond yields, rupee stability and softening crude prices further supported sentiment, while hope of possible reconsideration of equity taxation added to risk appetite.” The near-term sustainability of the rally would now depend on corporate earnings for the July-Sept quarter, and evidence of return of foreign funds, Nair said.During the day’s session, foreign funds emerged net sellers at Rs 5,285 crore, while domestic funds were net buyers at Rs 3,319 crore, BSE data showed. Private banks and IT stocks gained most.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: New inflows into gold FoFs halted by fund houses
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The mutual fund industry, on verbal instructions from markets regulator Sebi on Thursday evening, stopped fresh inflows into all gold fund of
articles.body: MUMBAI: The mutual fund industry, on verbal instructions from markets regulator Sebi on Thursday evening, stopped fresh inflows into all gold fund of funds (FoFs) that feed into gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs), effective Friday. However, all gold ETFs by these fund houses will continue to be traded on the bourses, several mutual fund officials told TOI.Currently, estimates show that the total industry size for gold ETFs is about Rs 1.7 lakh crore, of which a third of the assets are through the FoF route. "ETFs are the mother ship, FoFs feed into that," said a top fund manager.Late on Thursday, Tata Mutual Fund said that it was putting some temporary restrictions on lump-sum purchases, new systematic investment plans (SIPs) and systematic transfer plan (STP) registrations for Tata Gold ETF Fund of Fund, effective Oct 16, 2026.The fund house also said that instalments under existing SIP/STP registrations (registered prior to the effective date) shall continue and be processed at applicable net asset value. "(During) this suspension period, redemptions, switch-out, existing systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) will continue to be permitted," the release said. "The aforesaid suspension is temporary in nature."Industry players feel that given the size of the gold ETF in India, about 2% of the total MF industry's assets under management, the decision to suspend inflows into Gold FoFs cannot act as a game changer for the demand for the yellow metal in India.Of late, as govt tried to restrict gold imports which drains out precious foreign currency reserves from the country, it increased import duty on the yellow metal to 15%, from about 7-8% earlier.You use AI every day. articles.title: Online festive sales: Lower AOVs, bigger share of purchases through EMIs
articles.summary: MUMBAI: India’s online festive sales are somewhat missing the fiery spark this year.
articles.body: MUMBAI: India’s online festive sales are somewhat missing the fiery spark this year. Price hikes have weighed on smartphone sales volumes, typically the biggest driver of the season with final prices in many cases higher than last year even after discounts. Price increases have also made durables costlier with the share of large-ticket purchases (overall) through EMIs having significantly gone up this year—on Amazon, for instance, purchases using no-cost EMIs have jumped to 50% from about 30% last year, said Aman Deep Lohan, director, home, kitchen and outdoors at Amazon India. Amid inflation shrinking household budgets, smaller-ticket items found more space in shopping carts with consumers prioritising value for money. At the end of a week’s sales, average order values (AOV) are lower with growth having been led by categories such as fashion, beauty, home and general merchandise.“Value commerce, which covers items priced below Rs 500, handled about half of all festive orders. AOVs are 7-8% lower than last year because the basket moved to lower-ticket categories and channels. By value, phones and electronics still lead; by growth, softlines lead,” said Nikhil Dalal, associate partner, Redseer Strategy Consultants, which captured data from Oct 8-12. On Flipkart, about 7 in 10 units sold were priced under Rs 500.Unlike other seasons when a major chunk of the sales happen during Navaratri (the first leg of sale), analysts expect sales this year to be more spread out through Diwali as consumers strike a balance between their pockets and desire to buy. Estimates from Datum Intelligence showed that sales dropped by about 7-10% in the first four opening days to Rs 29,800-30,900 crore. “Last year’s sales opened on Sept 22, the day the GST rate cuts took effect. This year’s opening had no such trigger,” analysts at the firm said.Shrinking discounts, bigger EMIsAs price hikes shrunk the quantum of discounts on offer, particularly in demand-heavy categories such as smartphones, consumers went bigger on EMIs to buy premium products. “Phones entered the sale with average prices about 15% higher than a year ago. so even a similar headline discount leaves the final price above last year’s festive price. Across devices, sale-day prices were only about 5% to 10% below pre-sale levels, depending on category. Discounts were deeper where inventory and competition allowed: smartwatches and smart rings about 10%-15% below pre-sale prices, and some budget phones 10-15%,” Dalal said. Consumers opted for EMIs to buy 55-inch television sets, premium laptops and make other upgrades, said Lohan. Flipkart has also enabled cross-category exchanges—for instance, an old laptop can be traded for a new phone. “EMIs and bank offers saw increased adoption, signifying how customers are leveraging affordability options for their purchases this festive season,” said a Myntra spokesperson.Small town shoppers lead the festive queueWith the coverage of the internet and smartphones expanding, more small town consumers are taking to online shopping. What also helps is the wider availability of brands on e-commerce platforms. On Flipkart, consumers from places such as Sardulgarh, Panskura and Kishanganj logged in, making up some of the fastest-growing markets at the opening of the sale. About 60-65% of orders on Amazon came from tier 2 and 3 markets.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Fairfax does not cut jobs, more avenues likely: Prem Watsa
articles.summary: India-born Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, whose group Fairfax won the bid to buy 60.7% in IDBI Bank, is upbeat about India and its prospects.
articles.body: India-born Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, whose group Fairfax won the bid to buy 60.7% in IDBI Bank, is upbeat about India and its prospects. He discusses the way forward for the bank and synergies with Go Digit and IIFL. Excerpts:It’s been a long wait since the process started. How do you view the acquisition and how will it fit into your overall scheme of things?This is the biggest acquisition we’ve ever made. This is because we think India is the place to be, the Indian economy is going to do really well with the goal of Viksit Bharat and $30 trillion by 2047. The next two decades are going to be huge for India, particularly with the fact that you’ve got free trade (pacts). The Prime Minister and Piyush Goyal are negotiating deals with so many countries. This means you can make in India and sell it to the world. India has got great people, the engineers are so good. You have so many Indian CEOs leading global corporations. There’s going to be massive money flowing into India, from the US, Canada, Europe, Japan, from all over the world. There’s going to be a glorious time for everybody with huge employment. The banking system will benefit. China had a period like that from 2000 to 2010, with 10-11% real growth. India is at that level. Now, the focus will be on India.What are your plans for IDBI Bank?We’ve got property insurance, life insurance through Go Digit, which is going there (to IDBI). Wealth management and investment banking, which are with IIFL, are also going there. You’ve got a very powerful combination there with focus on customers and on providing outstanding service. We can attract pretty much anyone to join IDBI Bank. Rakesh (Sharma) is going to build that. It has 2,000 branches but it hasn’t expanded a lot due to the challenges it faced. All that has been dealt with.What will be your message to employees, some of whom are unsure about the future?Over 40 years, Fairfax has treated employees better than almost any company you can think of. We follow the golden rule which is to treat people like you want to be treated yourself. We have never laid off 5% or 10% of the staff. We’re going to work with them and we’re going to have this huge growth opportunity, which means you need people. The service conditions and their other benefits will, of course, remain. When Covid came, we never changed any benefits, we never changed any bonuses, not one person was let go of during that time.You have announced plans for Go Digit, IIFL Capital Services today. Will the exercise also involve restructuring of some of the IDBI subsidiaries and what is the road map for CSB Bank?We have got two years. So, we are going to look at that carefully, as soon as we close (the IDBI transaction). But we see insurance opportunities for banking clients and banking opportunities for insurance clients and the same for IIFL Capital. We have very good people, we believe in decentralised operations but working together. That’s how Fairfax was built. We see that taking place in IDBI Bank over time.Will you have a holding company structure, you have life, general insurance and reinsurance?Go Digit will be independent. It’ll have a board and will be independently run by Kamesh (Goyal). IIFL will be run by Venkat, Vasu and Nirmal. We weren’t going to change the structure in any way: no change in IIFL Capital, no change in Go Digit.The RBI mandate is to reduce your holding in IDBI to 40% in 10 years and to 26% in 15 years. What will be the dilution plan?We are focused on building the bank. Also, remember that when we began the insurance business it was 26% (FDI cap), which increased to 49% then to 74% and now it’s at 100%. We’ll see what happens in the future. We will go by whatever the regulations are at that point of time.Given the large diaspora in Canada, do you want to use the Canada-India corridor and have some IDBI branches there?No. My focus will be on India first. It has such a big market, 1.5 billion people. There are around 300 million people in the middle class, which is likely to double in 10 years. The US population is around 350 million. So, you go from 300 to 600 million, and there is going to be so much demand for all the services: the accounts, insurance. If you look at Singapore, when Lee Kuan Yew was first elected, apart from real estate, banking was the best investment option, it compounded 20% for the longest time. Once an economy is a developed economy, it doesn’t grow like that. It’s unbelievable how banking is needed. It’s the lifeline for any economy.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Irdai looking at ways to help policyholders stay the course
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Irdai is exploring ways to finance life insurance premiums against policy surrender values to help policyholders avoid premature surrenders and
articles.body: MUMBAI: Irdai is exploring ways to finance life insurance premiums against policy surrender values to help policyholders avoid premature surrenders and retain policies until maturity, chairman Ajay Seth said at Samvaad 2026, organised by Sahamati, the self-regulatory organisation for account aggregators.Many policyholders surrender policies when they need money or face a temporary income shortfall, particularly those outside the salaried workforce. Financing the final few premium instalments could help them retain the policy and realise better value at maturity, while giving lenders an existing policy value as security. "A significant number of policyholders surrender their policies because they need money. Another situation arises when income varies, particularly among people who are not salaried," Seth said. "Financing those final instalments could be useful. If the premiums are paid over time, the policyholder can realise better value, while the lender has an embedded value to rely on."Seth said a grey market had emerged for policy assignments, which he said were not permitted under the Insurance Act. "We could develop a formal channel for premium financing instead," he said. Irdai is also examining financing for health insurance premiums, which can be difficult for households with limited monthly incomes to pay upfront.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Mistry's tenure over, no basis to challenge Trusts' functioning'
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Mehli Mistry has no standing to challenge how two Tata trusts are run, the trusts told the charity commissioner's office on Thursday.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Mehli Mistry has no standing to challenge how two Tata trusts are run, the trusts told the charity commissioner's office on Thursday. Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Bai Hirabai Jamestji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution said Mistry's trusteeship tenure ended on Oct 28 last year, so he could not use it to challenge their administration and governance.In its affidavit, Bai Hirabai disputed Mistry's reading of Clauses 6 and 18 of its Trust Deed, which set eligibility for trusteeship by religion and residence. It argued that these restrictions conflict with the original Will and Codicil governing the Trust and should not be given effect. Bai Hirabai also filed a substitution application to name Noel Tata as reporting trustee in the matter related to Mistry's complaints on the trust's affairs, after Vijay Singh ceased to be a trustee earlier this year.Mistry responded with a submission on Thursday, asking Bai Hirabai to file an affidavit stating that Noel Tata met the eligibility criteria."It is submitted that the deputy Charity Commissioner shall ensure that the reporting trustee (Noel) proposed to be substituted by way of the present application shall be a qualified Trustee as contemplated in Clauses 6 and 18 of the Trust Deed dated Dec 7, 1923, which inter alia states that trustee shall be a Parsi professing Zoroastrian religion," Mistry said in his submission.Mistry claimed that Bai Hirabai's board included trustees who were ineligible because they did not meet the criteria in the trust deed, which required a trustee to be a permanent resident of Mumbai or Navsari and to belong to the Zoroastrian Parsi faith. In a separate hearing, the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) also told the charity commissioner that the office's May 15 order, which bars it from holding any meetings, created challenges for its functioning.You use AI every day. articles.title: Facing headwinds, Air India sharpens cost control focus
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Air India MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam has set up a “multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost savings team” to find all possible ways and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Air India MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam has set up a “multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost savings team” to find all possible ways and means of reducing expenditure on “full-time basis” amid mounting losses. Air India reported a loss of about $2.3 billion in 2025-26, the biggest annual loss since the Tata Group acquired the airline along with AI Express in Jan 2022. Overall, since then the airline has lost about $5.7 billion due to a combination of both internal and external factors.“While many external factors remain beyond our control, how we manage costs is something each of us can influence every day. Cost saving… requires active participation and commitment of every employee… Alongside operational excellence, we need to embed a mindset of frugality, accountability, and thoughtful decision-making in everything we do. We should continually challenge ourselves to ask – is this expenditure necessary? Is there a more efficient way to achieve the same outcome? Small decisions, taken consistently across organisation, can collectively strengthen financial resilience,” said Tewolde.While airlines globally have been facing elevated oil prices since the West Asia crisis along with other geopolitical challenges, Indian carriers have been worse off due to the rupee crashing and Pakistan airspace closure only for them. For Air India, the situation is even worse post the deadly Ahmedabad crash last June.“…a multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost saving team has been established on full-time basis to identify cost-saving opportunities across the organisation. They will systematically review all expenditure and identify cost-saving opportunities across functions,” his memo says.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Rupee gains 20 paise against US dollar as RBI support kicks in, greenback weakens
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rupee began Friday on a strong note, gaining 20 paise from its previous close to 94.79 against the US dollar.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rupee began Friday on a strong note, gaining 20 paise from its previous close to 94.79 against the US dollar. The rise came as American currency weakened and the impact of the Reserve Bank of India's structural forex interventions supported the unit.The gains, however, remained limited amid elevated crude oil prices and a negative beginning at Dalal Street.In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee began the session at 94.75 before moving to 94.79. The gain follows Thursday's 18-paise appreciation, which took the currency to a closing level of 94.99 against the dollar.Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, told PTI, "Decline in dollar index and softening of US treasury yields also supported the rupee. However, a surge in crude oil prices capped sharp gains. On the data front, US PPI (Producer Price Index) was hotter than expected while retail sales topped forecast. Weekly unemployment claims were in line with expectations."The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six currencies, fell 0.54% to 102. US Treasury yields also eased, providing support to rupee.Meanwhile in the commodity market Brent crude futures were trading 0.54% lower at $105.35 per barrel.Domestic equities remained under pressure in early trade.BSE Sensex opened 113 points down at 74,187, while NSE Nifty50 slipped 27.20 points to 22,967.15. However, both indices turned green later in the session, with Sensex gaining 400 points and Nifty50 topping 23,100.Adding to the market backdrop, Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net sellers of domestic equities worth Rs 5,285.37 crore on Thursday, exchange data showed.You use AI every day.
